check.answer: The NAME of B is 'bee' (the word you hear when you sing the ABC song). The SOUND of B is /b/ — short, like the start of 'ball'. When you read, you use the SOUND, not the name. If you tried to read 'bag' by names, you'd say 'bee-ay-gee' — which doesn't sound like 'bag'. You read 'bag' by sounds: /b/ /æ/ /g/ — that blends into 'bag'.
check.prompt: What's the difference between the NAME of a letter and the SOUND of a letter? Use B as an example.
check.teaching_note: This is the single most-missed concept at the start of phonics. Many children learn the alphabet song (names) before they learn sounds, then get stuck. Practice with letters they know names for: 'I know the NAME — what's the SOUND?' Until the sounds are automatic, every other phonics unit is harder.

unit.decodable_sentence: Each letter has a sound. Say the sound, not the name.
examples: C says /k/ — cat, cup, cot (soft /s/ comes later, as in cent)
G says /g/ — go, gum, gas (soft /j/ comes later, as in gem)
Vowels SHORT: A /æ/ apple, E /ɛ/ egg, I /ɪ/ inch, O /ɒ/ octopus, U /ʌ/ umbrella
M says /m/, N says /n/ — common but easy to confuse if quiet
S says /s/ snake; Z says /z/ zip; the /s/ and /z/ are close — feel your throat
Y is sometimes a consonant (yes) and sometimes a vowel (sky, baby)

modes.instruction: Adult shows a letter, says the sound (not the name), and gives an example word. 'B — /b/ — ball.' Run through all consonants and the five short vowels.
modes.label: Coach says the sound
modes.script: This is B. It says /b/. Like ball, bag, bed. Your turn: /b/.

modes.instruction: Adult holds a letter card; child says the sound. Then swap — child shows a letter; adult says the sound (occasionally wrong on purpose so child corrects).
modes.label: Take turns
modes.script: What sound does this letter make? (Hold up D.) Now you pick a letter for me.

modes.instruction: Child sees a letter and says the sound. Stuck → Echo (adult says it first), then Phonics (give an example word starting with that letter), then Repeat.
modes.label: I say
modes.script: What sound? (Show letters one at a time.)

unit.note: Coach finds and presents the lesson; it never generates it, and never grades a child.
unit.rule: Each letter of the alphabet stands for one or more SOUNDS, not just a name. Before you can read words, you need the letter-sound link. Consonants mostly say their main sound: B says /b/ as in 'ball'. Vowels (A, E, I, O, U, sometimes Y) have two main sounds each — short and long. Today we learn the consonants and the SHORT vowel sound for each vowel. Long vowels come later (with magic-e and vowel teams).
unit.subject: read
unit.summary: Letter-sound correspondence — the precursor to all decoding. Twenty-six consonants + five short vowel sounds. The check distinguishes letter NAME (bee) from letter SOUND (/b/) — the most-missed concept at the start of reading.
